extracted.intended_audience: ML and AI practitioners, model developers, software engineers, policymakers, organizations, and other stakeholders involved in developing, deploying, or using trained machine learning models
extracted.subtask_short: model card reporting for ML models
extracted.subtask_description: Create short (one- to two-page) model documentation ('model cards') that describe a trained machine learning model's intended uses, performance (including disaggregated evaluation across groups, environments, and instrumentation), training/evaluation data, metrics, ethical considerations, caveats, and recommendations. The goal is to enable stakeholders to assess a model's suitability, fairness, and risks prior to deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model card length and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards are short (one to two page) records accompanying trained machine learning models that provide benchmarked evaluation in a variety of conditions and disclose the context in which models are intended to be used, details of the performance evaluation procedures, and other relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise documentation to clarify intended use cases and minimize usage in contexts for which models are not well suited; complement Datasheets for Datasets and other documentation paradigms; provide benchmarked evaluation across cultural, demographic, phenotypic, and intersectional groups relevant to the intended application domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Details — person or organization developing model
rubrics_metrics.description: What person or organization developed the model?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide author/owner information so stakeholders can infer development context and potential conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Details — model date
rubrics_metrics.description: When was the model developed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include development date to inform stakeholders about likely available techniques and data sources at time of development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Details — model version
rubrics_metrics.description: Which version of the model is it, and how does it differ from previous versions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Versioning helps track updates, associate known bugs to correct versions, and aid comparisons across models; update the model card with each release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Details — model type
rubrics_metrics.description: What type of model is it (e.g., Naive Bayes, Convolutional Neural Network)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include architecture and basic model details to help technical users understand encoded assumptions; provide paper/resources for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Details — training algorithms, parameters, fairness constraints, features
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about training algorithms, parameters, fairness constraints or other applied approaches, and features used in the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose what can be shared without compromising proprietary secrets; this helps developers and ML-knowledgeable individuals evaluate assumptions and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Details — citation, license, feedback contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide paper or other resource for more information, citation details, license, and where to send questions or comments about the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give pointers to further info and a contact to allow stakeholders to follow up or request clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended Use — primary intended uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary intended uses: tasks or purposes the model was developed for (e.g., plant recognition worldwide or in the Pacific Northwest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about the scope and granularity of intended tasks; this frames downstream statistical analyses and suitability judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended Use — primary intended users
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary intended users: e.g., entertainment, hobbyists, enterprise solutions, policymakers, impacted individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stating intended users helps evaluate robustness expectations and which stakeholder decisions the card should inform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended Use — out-of-scope uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Out-of-scope use cases: contexts or tasks for which the model should not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List contexts the model might be confused with and recommend alternative models where appropriate; inspired by warning labels to prevent misuse (examples: 'not for use on text examples shorter than 100 tokens').

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors — relevant factors (groups, instrumentation, environments)
rubrics_metrics.description: What are foreseeable salient factors for which model performance may vary (e.g., demographic/phenotypic groups, camera hardware, lighting conditions)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine relevant factors by examining intended use and deployment context; include groups, instrumentation, and environment as primary factor types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors — evaluation factors (which are reported and why)
rubrics_metrics.description: Which factors are being reported, and why were these chosen? If relevant factors and evaluation factors differ, explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain selection criteria for reported factors and note limitations where certain factor annotations are unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groups — definition, annotation provenance, and privacy considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: For human-centric models, groups are people who share one or multiple characteristics (cultural, demographic, phenotypic). Specify who annotated datasets, annotation instructions and compensation, inter-annotator agreement, and whether labels are self-identified or perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance utility of group analyses with privacy/sensitivity concerns; collaborate with policy, privacy, and legal experts; when possible prefer self-identified labels or clearly designate labels as perceived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groups — intersectional analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide intersectional analyses combining two (or more) groups/conditions (e.g., age and race) to surface compounded disparities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine intersectional groups based on intended use; intersectional analyses highlight harms that unitary analyses can miss and are linked to intersectionality theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumentation — capture hardware/software details
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the instruments used to capture inputs (e.g., camera lens, image stabilization, aperture, microphone), since performance may vary across instrumentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include hardware/software settings that materially affect inputs and model behavior to help users anticipate deployment differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment — deployment environmental conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe environmental factors (e.g., lighting, humidity) that may affect model performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specifications across different environments to help users understand impacts and limitations (e.g., face detection less accurate under low lighting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics — select model performance measures appropriate to model and real-world impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The reported metrics should be determined based on the model’s structure and intended use and should reflect potential real-world impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why chosen metrics were selected over alternatives and how they map to stakeholder priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics — decision thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: If decision thresholds are used, state what they are and why they were chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presented digitally, provide a threshold slider to view performance across thresholds; document thresholds used in reported metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics — approaches to uncertainty and variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how measurements and estimations are calculated (e.g., standard deviation, variance, confidence intervals, KL divergence) and how approximations were obtained (e.g., number of runs, cross-validation folds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report uncertainty measures and methods (bootstrap, cross-validation) so readers can judge statistical reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification systems — confusion-matrix-based error metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: For classification systems, report error types derivable from a confusion matrix: false positive rate, false negative rate, false discovery rate, and false omission rate; the relative importance of each is system-, product- and context-dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List all confusion-matrix values and provide context on which were prioritized during development and why; note parity relationships to formal fairness definitions (e.g., Equality of Opportunity, Equality of Odds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Score-based analyses — distributional and divergence metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: For score-based systems, report distribution measures (mode, median, mean, range, quartiles, variance, standard deviation) and other differences such as cross entropy, perplexity, KL divergence, and pinned AUC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider comparing score distributions across groups; extend beyond summary statistics when useful (e.g., pinned AUC for toxicity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Task-specific score metrics (translation/speech etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: For tasks that output non-scalar labels (e.g., translation, speech recognition), compare task-relevant scores across groups (e.g., BLEU for translation, word-error rate for speech recognition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if primary outputs are not scores, group-wise score comparisons can yield meaningful insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence intervals and reporting for disaggregated metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide confidence intervals for reported metrics, especially for metrics disaggregated by combinations of instrumentation, environments, and groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate CIs using appropriate statistical methods (e.g., bootstrap resampling, treat confusion matrices probabilistically) and present error bars in visualizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Data — list datasets used and link to documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: State what datasets were used to evaluate the model and point to documents that provide source and composition visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer evaluation datasets that are publicly available for third-party use; reference dataset documentation (e.g., Datasheets for Datasets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Data — motivation for dataset choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why particular evaluation datasets were chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose datasets representative of typical use cases and also include anticipated test scenarios and challenging cases to reveal pathological issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Data — preprocessing details
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how data was preprocessed for evaluation (e.g., tokenization, image cropping, filtering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document preprocessing steps so results are reproducible and evaluable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Data — representativeness and complementary challenging sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Include evaluation sets that match expected deployment populations and separate challenging datasets (e.g., children, elderly, out-of-domain populations) to surface failure modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluating both matched and challenging sets helps identify issues not evident in routine testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Data — synthetic data usage and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: When real-world data are unrepresentative or unavailable, synthetic datasets may be used to provide coverage for otherwise unevaluated use cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document synthetic data generation methods and recognize synthetic data covers limited cases; use with caution and note limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Data — provide as much information as feasible or summary distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, mirror Evaluation Data information for Training Data; if not feasible, provide minimal allowable information such as distribution over various factors in the training datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If training data are proprietary, at least disclose distributional summaries to help stakeholders reason about encoded biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative Analyses — disaggregated reporting (unitary and intersectional results)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative analyses should be disaggregated (broken down) by chosen factors and include unitary (single-factor) and intersectional (multi-factor) results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate metric variation (e.g., with error bars) and provide confidence intervals; parity across subgroups on metrics corresponds to some fairness definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative Analyses — show metric variation and visualizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate metric variation (e.g., with error bars) and visualize disaggregated results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plots and error bars to convey variability and uncertainty clearly (example: Figure 2 in paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Considerations — data sensitivity and human-impact questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss ethical questions: Does the model use sensitive data (protected classes)? Is it intended to inform decisions about human life or flourishing? What mitigations were used? What risks and harms are present? Are there use-cases that are especially fraught?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surface ethical challenges and mitigation strategies, identify potential recipients/likelihood/magnitude of harms, and note if unknowns remain; include external review or community testing where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats and Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: List additional concerns not covered elsewhere (e.g., missing groups in evaluation, suggestions for further testing, ideal characteristics of an evaluation dataset).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about known limitations and actionable recommendations for model use or further evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning, maintenance, and change history
rubrics_metrics.description: Document how model behavior changes over time and keep the model card updated with each new model release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comparisons across versions (examples in paper: TOXICITY v.1 vs v.5) so stakeholders can track bias mitigation and overall changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency limits and complementary practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that model cards rely on the integrity of creators and are one transparency tool among many; they do not by themselves prevent misleading representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend complementary practices such as third-party quantitative/qualitative audits, adversarial testing, and inclusive user feedback mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder-targeted content (use-case-driven reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor model card content to inform different stakeholders (ML practitioners, developers, software engineers, policymakers, organizations, impacted individuals) about model suitability and risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sections and language that help each stakeholder group answer their specific questions (e.g., deployment suitability for organizations, remedial info for impacted individuals).
